checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.55pp larger on average (182 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: STATISTICAL REALITY states 'measured ghost arrival = 25.4 control trades/day', and confirm is planned at n=600.
findings.problem: The live tape shows only 19 live-tier events total and control live_n=2 across a 60.7-day data span. At 25.4 control trades/day the live tier would hold thousands of events, not 19. Either the 25.4/day figure is measured on the backfill stream and mislabelled as live arrival, or the live counter is broken. Any schedule to reach confirm n=600 built on 25.4/day is wrong by orders of magnitude, and no n is reported behind the 25.4 figure.

findings.claim: Checklist 'bonferroni_monotonic' is green: 'Corrected bar counts every question asked — lifetime tests=6, pre-registered hypotheses=6; alpha=0.00833'.
findings.problem: The graveyard shows sl-entry-anchor was actually run and killed on a paired test at n=1474 with p=9.18e-41 judged 'vs alpha=0.01250'. An alpha of 0.01250 implies a family of 4, while the current bar implies 6. So the family grew after that test was scored and the earlier verdict was never re-judged at the tighter bar, and the three retired screen arms (dedup-24h, dedup-48h, sl-entry-anchor) are not visible in the count of 6. The checkbox title asserts every question asked is counted; the numbers on the page disagree with each other.

findings.claim: Checklist 'backfill_cannot_promote' is green: 'Only live-tape evidence can promote — 0 surfaced arm(s); none promoted from a screen'.
findings.problem: This is vacuously true and establishes nothing: with zero arms ever surfaced the gate has never been exercised once. Meanwhile every number the arena reports — screen_wr, screen_ev, screen_dWR at screen_n between 494 and 1539 — comes from the tier with 4764 backfill events versus 19 live. A green tick here reads as 'promotion evidence is clean' when what it actually says is 'nothing has happened yet'.

findings.claim: 'entry_granularity_declared': the kernel reads pumps +0.55pp larger than live on 182 matched setups, but 'Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel'.
findings.problem: The shared-kernel argument only holds for arms whose changed parameter is orthogonal to the mismeasured quantity. entry-8pct changes pump_pct, which is exactly the quantity carrying the +0.55pp bias, so the bias is not common-mode for that arm: it shifts which events clear 8.0 versus which clear 5.0 differently, and entry-8pct's screen_n=494 is itself a product of the biased measurement. The validity claim is asserted for all arms when it is not established for the entry_trigger arm.

findings.claim: Checklist 'arms_running' is green and critical: 'Variant arms are live in the arena — 5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x'.
findings.problem: Running here is registry status, not traded evidence. Those five arms carry live_n of 2, 2, 1, 1 and 2 respectively, with declined counts of 13 to 18 each. A critical green labelled 'live in the arena' is being satisfied by metadata while the live sample is one or two trades per arm — the exact inversion the project's own methodology flags via firstred-1h, where status metadata was allowed to outrank the trading record.

findings.claim: Checklist 'no_lookahead' is green and critical: 'Detection is look-ahead free — re-detected 108 events on truncated history across 6 coins; mismatches: none'.
findings.problem: The check covers 108 of 4783 shared-window events and 6 of 176 coins, roughly 2% of events and 3% of coins, yet is reported as establishing that detection as a whole is look-ahead free. A clean result on that slice is consistent with look-ahead confined to coins or event types outside it — note that the kernel_agreement misses cluster on BOME, a name whose behaviour the no_lookahead sample is not shown to include.
